election._note: Federal, regional and EP elections are held together every 5 years in June (2024 was 9 June, alongside the EP vote); Wikipedia '2024 Belgian federal election'

dissolution._note: The King may dissolve the Chamber only when the federal Government resigns with the consent of an absolute majority of the Chamber, or when the Chamber rejects a confidence motion or carries a no-confidence motion without proposing a successor PM within three days. No confidence-vote command exists at V1.1c, so this refuses the player's command outright. senate.be, 'Introduction in Belgian Parliamentary History'; archive.ipu.org, 'Motion of censure and votes of no confidence'.

amendment._note: A revision requires declaring the relevant article open to revision, dissolving Parliament, and re-electing it before the new Chambers can amend it by a 2/3 majority with a 2/3 quorum present. The dissolution-and-re-election step is not modelled; the entrenching number, 2/3, is what this rule carries. senate.be, 'Revision of the Constitution'.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: Nothing in the Belgian constitution excludes the monarchy from ordinary revision -- the crown itself is a revisable title, not an entrenched one.

formation._note: Government formed by coalition negotiation and appointed by the King; requires the confidence of the Chamber, carried on a simple majority of those voting.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2023-2024, rounded. V1.2a starting policy, derived from France's anchor (see FRA.json): VAT 21% is Belgium's own statutory standard rate (Tax Foundation, 'VAT Rates in Europe 2024'). Income is France's 20 scaled by Belgium's OECD Revenue Statistics personal-tax-to-GDP share against France's -- Belgium carries one of the OECD's heaviest personal income tax loads, hence 24; corporate stays close to France's own at 25. Spending is France's split scaled by general government expenditure of 54.1% of GDP against France's 57.3% (TheGlobalEconomy.com / OECD Government at a Glance 2025).
